summary: Thierry Mathou specializes in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Sciences Po and EDHEC Business School and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He completed his PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003). He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006) and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya and teachers Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinlay Ram Shashni works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as an editor (attested 1997, 2007) and later as Associate Professor and IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).
Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje), and he founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago Divinity School under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1980–1986) under William R. Hutchison and others, and he served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).
Thomas Athol Joyce worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Hertford College (~1897–1901) and held a post at the British Museum from around 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Blom Hansen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Aalborg University. He held positions at the University of Natal, Edinburgh, Yale, and Amsterdam, before becoming Professor of Anthropology at Stanford University in 2010.

Thomas Borchert specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. A PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005) who studied under Bruce Lincoln and others, he served as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai. He held posts at the British Museum and SOAS before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit and fellow at Oxford (1944–1976).

Thomas Christian Tychsen worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University (~1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1783), where he later held an academic post from around 1788 to 1834.
Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earning a Ph.D. from Harvard University and a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne, supervised by Tom Tillemans and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow is an art historian educated at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor at NYU in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Eton and East India Company College, and under Jagannatha, he served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.
Thomas Ethelbert Page worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He was educated at Shrewsbury School and St John's College (~1869–1873) and held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD, 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman, he served as Executive Editor at Columbia University (attested 2007).
